headline: Apple's updated App Store rules more explicitly ban apps that use AI to make nonconsensual intimate images and say developers who do not prevent them may be removed.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a confirmed rule change by a major platform, but the report gives no detail on how strictly it will be enforced.
importance_line: People targeted by AI-made fake intimate images, especially women and children, gain a clearer rule and app developers now carry a duty to prevent such images, but Apple did not pull X or Grok and it is not yet clear how strictly the rules will be enforced.
summary: The Verge reports that Apple's updated App Store rules, announced on 16 Oct 2026, more explicitly ban "nudify" apps, which use AI to generate intimate images of people without their consent, and require developers to "proactively prevent and remove" such images or risk removal from the store. The changes follow criticism of Apple after X users used the Grok chatbot earlier this year to make nonconsensual sexualized deepfakes, including of minors, and a July order from a San Francisco city attorney to remove 13 such apps, which Apple said it did.
notes: Short Verge article; enforcement details not given.
